name: Ezekiel
role: Priest and prophet among the exiles in Babylon
whenBasis: His dated oracles run from the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile (1:2) to the twenty-seventh (29:17).
summary: A priest, son of Buzi, taken to Babylon with Jehoiachin, who saw the glory of the LORD by the Kebar canal: living creatures, wheels full of eyes, and a throne like sapphire. He acted out the siege of Jerusalem, lay on his side for months, shaved his head and divided his hair, and was forbidden to mourn when his wife died. After the city fell he saw a valley of dry bones live and a new temple with a river flowing from it.
body: He is made a watchman for Israel, given a scroll to eat that tastes like honey, and struck dumb except when the LORD opens his mouth. In a vision he is taken to Jerusalem and sees idolatry in the temple and the glory of the LORD leaving it.

His oracles against Tyre and Egypt, his parable of the two sisters, and his teaching that each person bears his own sin fill the middle of the book. When a fugitive brings word that the city has fallen, his mouth is opened. The LORD asks him, “Son of man, can these bones come to life?” He ends with the measured plan of a new temple and land; the Models tab draws that temple.
